author:	ojcchar
association:	contributor

Hi @all,

We posted two options for your team's feature for Sprints 3 and 4. Please select one of them to develop:

- https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa/issues/100 (hold stock for shoppers during checkout)
- https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa/issues/101 (product bundles with their own price)

A few things you should consider:

1. Complete the spec. The issue is a starting point: the acceptance criteria are incomplete and the open questions need answers. We expect thorough specs that cover what happens when things go wrong (invalid input, failures, conflicts, permissions, old data), not only the main path. The open questions are not a complete list; find the other cases too.
2. Given the scope of the issue, split the feature into sub-issues. Your breakdown should cover the areas listed in the issue.
3. Plan which sub-issues go in Sprint 3. Post your breakdown as a comment on the issue. Each sub-issue should have an owner, a full spec, and a spec review.
4. By the end of Sprint 3 (Nov 19), deliver a working part of the feature that we can demo end-to-end, through the admin dashboard and the store API. It doesn't need to be complete, but it must work as a whole, not as separate pieces that aren't connected yet.

Treat us as your customer. If anything is unclear or you need a decision about the expected behavior, ask us on the issue or on Zulip. Don't guess; ask.

Cheers,
--
author:	njpiombino

@musta55 @ojcchar A few quick questions. Can a shopper return just one item from a bundle? If yes, how is the refund worked out: proportional to each component's normal price, a fixed amount set per component, or decided by the admin on each return? If a product in a bundle is deleted, should the deletion be blocked while bundles use it, or should the bundle be automatically unpublished? Should a bundle appear in the storefront as a normal product, with its own page, images and place in category listings? Or only on a dedicated bundles page or as an upsell on the component products?
--
author:	ojcchar
association:	contributor
edited:	false
status:	none
--
@njpiombino 

1. Yes, a shopper can return just one item from a bundle. The refund is proportional to each item's normal price. For example, if the camera, lens, and bag normally cost $800, $300, and $100, the bag is 1/12 of the kit, so returning it refunds 1/12 of the bundle price. Make sure the shares add up exactly to the bundle price after rounding. If Medusa's return flow already lets admins adjust a refund amount, admins can still adjust it on a specific return.
2. Block the deletion and show which bundles use the product (or variant). The admin must remove it from those bundles first. Past orders that include the bundle must keep working.
3. A bundle should behave like a normal product in the store API: its own title, images, price, and categories, so any storefront can show it on its own page and in category listings. A dedicated bundles page or upsells on component products are out of scope.
--

{"body":"## Summary\nThis adds backend support for bundles: products made from several component variants, sold at their own price. A bundle behaves like any other product in the store API, with its own title, images, price and categories, and buying one reduces stock for each component. Store owners can then sell kits and deals, and shoppers can buy related items together in one purchase.\n\n## User Story\nAs a store owner, I want to create a bundle from several product variants with its own price so that I can sell kits and deals.\n\n## User Scenario\nThe store owner sends a request to create a \"Camera kit\" bundle with a title, images and the \"Cameras\" category, containing 1x camera body, 1x lens and 1x bag, priced at $899 in USD and €849 in EUR. The kit shows up on its own product page and in the Cameras category like any other product. Shoppers can add it to their cart, and buying it reduces stock for all three components. Later, the owner tries to delete the lens product and gets an error saying it is used in \"Camera kit\".\n\n## Scope\nMedium: one new workflow and admin create/update routes built on the existing inventory-kit links, plus a check added to the existing product and variant delete workflows, with no new data model and no migration.\n\n## Source\nParent issue #101 (product bundles), from the project issue tracker.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. An admin can create a bundle by giving the normal product fields (title, description, images, categories), at least 2 component variants with a quantity for each, and prices per currency.\n2. An admin can update a bundle's product fields, components, quantities and prices.\n3. A bundle is returned by the store API like any other product: on its own and in category listings, with its title, images, price and categories.\n4. The store API marks a product as a bundle and lists its components (variant and quantity), so other code can look up a bundle's components.\n5. Placing an order for a bundle reduces stock for each component by its quantity multiplied by the number of bundles ordered.\n6. A bundle shows as out of stock if any component is out of stock. Its available quantity is the lowest number of complete bundles the component stock can make.\n7. A request is rejected with a clear error when:\n   - it has fewer than 2 components\n   - a component variant doesn't exist\n   - a component doesn't track inventory\n   - a component is itself a bundle\n   - the same component is listed twice\n   - a quantity is 0 or less\n   - a price is missing or negative\n8. A rejected create leaves no partial bundle behind (the workflow rolls back).\n9. Users who aren't logged in as an admin can't create or update bundles.\n10. A component's price changing does not change the bundle's price.\n11. Deleting a product or variant that is used in a bundle is blocked, with an error naming every bundle that uses it. Once it has been removed from those bundles, it can be deleted normally.\n12. Past orders that include a bundle keep working (viewing, fulfilling and returning) after the bundle is edited or deleted.\n13. Upgrading needs no data migration. Existing products, inventory kits and orders behave exactly as before.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Bundles inside bundles\n- Bundles built by the shopper (\"pick any 3\")\n- A dedicated bundles page or upsells on component products\n- Checkout errors, refund shares and returns (see the checkout and returns issue)\n- Admin UI (see the admin bundle screens issue)\n\n## Open Questions\n- Is there a maximum number of components per bundle, or is the minimum of 2 the only limit?\n- Should deleting the bundle itself be blocked while it has unfulfilled orders, or is that already safe because orders keep a copy of their line items?","comments":[],"labels":[],"state":"OPEN","title":"Add API to create and manage product bundles"}

A shopper buys the kit, and the store ships all three items.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria (draft, incomplete)\n\n- An admin can create a bundle from several product variants, with its own price.\n- Shoppers can add a bundle to their cart and buy it.\n- Placing an order deducts stock for each product in the bundle.\n- If any product in the bundle is out of stock, the order can't be placed and the shopper sees which product.\n- More criteria needed, based on the open questions below.\n\nAcceptance criteria should also cover invalid input, failures, conflicts, and permissions, not only the main path.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Bundles inside bundles\n- Bundles built by the shopper (\"pick any 3\")\n\n## Open Questions\n\n- How is availability shown when one product in the bundle is out of stock?\n- How do promotions and taxes apply to a bundle?\n- Can a customer return one product from a bundle? import { createLinksWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import { Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { refetchVariant } from "../../../../helpers"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
    HttpTypes.AdminCreateVariantInventoryItem,
    HttpTypes.SelectParams
  >,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductVariantResponse>
) => {
  const variantId = req.params.variant_id

  await createLinksWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: [
      {
        [Modules.PRODUCT]: { variant_id: variantId },
        [Modules.INVENTORY]: {
          inventory_item_id: req.validatedBody.inventory_item_id,
        },
        data: { required_quantity: req.validatedBody.required_quantity },
      },
    ],
  })

  const variant = await refetchVariant(
    variantId,
    req.scope,
    req.queryConfig.fields
  )

  res.status(200).json({ variant })
}
import { dismissLinksWorkflow, updateLinksWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import { Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { refetchVariant } from "../../../../../helpers"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
    HttpTypes.AdminUpdateVariantInventoryItem,
    HttpTypes.SelectParams
  >,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductVariantResponse>
) => {
  const variantId = req.params.variant_id
  const inventoryItemId = req.params.inventory_item_id

  await updateLinksWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: [
      {
        [Modules.PRODUCT]: { variant_id: variantId },
        [Modules.INVENTORY]: { inventory_item_id: inventoryItemId },
        data: { required_quantity: req.validatedBody.required_quantity },
      },
    ],
  })

  const variant = await refetchVariant(
    variantId,
    req.scope,
    req.queryConfig.fields
  )

  res.status(200).json({ variant })
}

export const DELETE = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<{}, HttpTypes.SelectParams>,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductVariantInventoryLinkDeleteResponse>
) => {
  const variantId = req.params.variant_id
  const inventoryItemId = req.params.inventory_item_id

  const {
    result: [deleted],
  } = await dismissLinksWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: [
      {
        [Modules.PRODUCT]: { variant_id: variantId },
        [Modules.INVENTORY]: { inventory_item_id: inventoryItemId },
      },
    ],
  })

  const parent = await refetchVariant(
    variantId,
    req.scope,
    req.queryConfig.fields
  )

  res.status(200).json({
    id: deleted as unknown as HttpTypes.AdminProductVariantInventoryLink,
    object: "variant-inventory-item-link",
    deleted: true,
    parent,
  })
}

import { batchLinksWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { buildBatchVariantInventoryData } from "../../../../helpers"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
    HttpTypes.AdminBatchVariantInventoryItems
  >,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductVariantInventoryBatchResponse>
) => {
  const { create = [], update = [], delete: toDelete = [] } = req.validatedBody

  const { result } = await batchLinksWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: {
      create: buildBatchVariantInventoryData(create),
      update: buildBatchVariantInventoryData(update),
      delete: buildBatchVariantInventoryData(toDelete),
    },
  })

  res.status(200).json({
    created: result.created,
    updated: result.updated,
    deleted: result.deleted,
  } as unknown as HttpTypes.AdminProductVariantInventoryBatchResponse)
}
    created: createdRes,
    updated: updatedRes,
    deleted: {
      ids: batchResult.deleted,
      object: "variant",
      deleted: true,
    },
  }
}

export const buildBatchVariantInventoryData = (
  inputs:
    | AdminBatchVariantInventoryItemsType["create"]
    | AdminBatchVariantInventoryItemsType["update"]
    | AdminBatchVariantInventoryItemsType["delete"]
) => {
  const results: LinkDefinition[] = []

  for (const input of inputs || []) {
    const result: LinkDefinition = {
      [Modules.PRODUCT]: { variant_id: input.variant_id },
      [Modules.INVENTORY]: {
        inventory_item_id: input.inventory_item_id,
      },
    }

    if ("required_quantity" in input) {
      result.data = {
        required_quantity: input.required_quantity,
      }
    }

    results.push(result)
  }

  return results
}

import {
  BigNumberInput,
  ConfirmVariantInventoryWorkflowInputDTO,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  BigNumber,
  MathBN,
  MedusaError,
  deepFlatMap,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"

export const requiredOrderFieldsForInventoryConfirmation = [
  "id",
  "version",
  "canceled_at",
  "sales_channel_id",
  "items.*",
  "items.variant.manage_inventory",
  "items.variant.allow_backorder",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory_item_id",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.required_quantity",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stocked_quantity",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.reserved_quantity",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.raw_stocked_quantity",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.raw_reserved_quantity",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.location_id",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.id",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.name",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.sales_channels.id",
  "items.variant.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.sales_channels.name",
]

export const requiredVariantFieldsForInventoryConfirmation = [
  "manage_inventory",
  "allow_backorder",
  "inventory_items.inventory_item_id",
  "inventory_items.required_quantity",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stocked_quantity",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.reserved_quantity",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.raw_stocked_quantity",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.raw_reserved_quantity",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.location_id",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.id",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.name",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.sales_channels.id",
  "inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.sales_channels.name",
]

interface ConfirmInventoryPreparationInput {
  product_variant_inventory_items: {
    variant_id: string
    inventory_item_id: string
    required_quantity: number
  }[]
  items: {
    id?: string
    variant_id?: string | null
    quantity: BigNumberInput
  }[]
  variants: {
    id: string
    manage_inventory?: boolean
    allow_backorder?: boolean
  }[]
  location_ids: string[]
  stockAvailability: Map<string, Map<string, BigNumberInput>>
}

interface ConfirmInventoryItem {
  id?: string
  inventory_item_id: string
  required_quantity: number
  allow_backorder: boolean
  quantity: BigNumberInput
  location_ids: string[]
}

/**
 * This function prepares the input for the confirm inventory workflow.
 * In essesnce, it maps a list of cart items to a list of inventory items,
 * serving as a bridge between the cart and inventory domains.
 *
 * @throws {MedusaError} INVALID_DATA if any cart item is for a variant that has no inventory items.
 * @throws {MedusaError} INVALID_DATA if any cart item is for a variant with no stock locations in the input.sales_channel_id. An exception is made for variants with allow_backorder set to true.
 *
 * @returns {ConfirmInventoryPreparationInput}
 * A list of inventory items to confirm. Only inventory items for variants with managed inventory are included.
 */
export const prepareConfirmInventoryInput = (data: {
  input: ConfirmVariantInventoryWorkflowInputDTO
}) => {
  const productVariantInventoryItems = new Map<string, any>()
  const stockLocationIds = new Set<string>()
  const allVariants = new Map<string, any>()
  const mapLocationAvailability = new Map<string, Map<string, BigNumberInput>>()
  const variantsWithLocationForChannel = new Set<string>()
  let hasManagedInventory = false

  const salesChannelId = data.input.sales_channel_id

  for (const updateItem of data.input.itemsToUpdate ?? []) {
    const updateItem_ = "data" in updateItem ? updateItem.data : updateItem

    const item = data.input.items.find(
      (item) => item.variant_id === updateItem_.variant_id
    )
    if (item && updateItem_.quantity) {
      item.quantity = updateItem_.quantity!
    }
  }

  deepFlatMap(
    data.input,
    "variants.inventory_items.inventory.location_levels.stock_locations.sales_channels",
    ({
      variants,
      inventory_items,
      location_levels,
      stock_locations,
      sales_channels,
    }) => {
      if (!variants) {
        return
      }

      if (salesChannelId && sales_channels?.id === salesChannelId) {
        variantsWithLocationForChannel.add(variants.id)
      }

      if (location_levels && inventory_items) {
        const availability = MathBN.sub(
          location_levels.raw_stocked_quantity ??
            location_levels.stocked_quantity ??
            0,
          location_levels.raw_reserved_quantity ??
            location_levels.reserved_quantity ??
            0
        )

        if (!mapLocationAvailability.has(location_levels.location_id)) {
          mapLocationAvailability.set(location_levels.location_id, new Map())
        }

        const locationMap = mapLocationAvailability.get(
          location_levels.location_id
        )!
        locationMap.set(
          inventory_items.inventory_item_id,
          new BigNumber(availability)
        )
      }

      if (stock_locations && sales_channels?.id === salesChannelId) {
        stockLocationIds.add(stock_locations.id)
      }

      if (inventory_items) {
        const inventoryItemId = inventory_items.inventory_item_id
        const mapKey = `${inventoryItemId}-${inventory_items.variant_id}`

        if (!productVariantInventoryItems.has(mapKey)) {
          productVariantInventoryItems.set(mapKey, {
            variant_id: inventory_items.variant_id,
            inventory_item_id: inventoryItemId,
            required_quantity: inventory_items.required_quantity,
          })
        }
      }

      if (!allVariants.has(variants.id)) {
        if (!hasManagedInventory && variants.manage_inventory) {
          hasManagedInventory = true
        }

        allVariants.set(variants.id, {
          id: variants.id,
          manage_inventory: variants.manage_inventory,
          allow_backorder: variants.allow_backorder,
        })
      }
    }
  )

  if (!hasManagedInventory) {
    return { items: [] }
  }

  if (salesChannelId) {
    for (const variant of allVariants.values()) {
      if (
        variant.manage_inventory &&
        !variantsWithLocationForChannel.has(variant.id) &&
        !variant.allow_backorder
      ) {
        throw new MedusaError(
          MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
          `Sales channel ${salesChannelId} is not associated with any stock location for variant ${variant.id}.`
        )
      }
    }
  }

  const items = formatInventoryInput({
    product_variant_inventory_items: Array.from(
      productVariantInventoryItems.values()
    ),
    location_ids: Array.from(stockLocationIds),
    stockAvailability: mapLocationAvailability,
    items: data.input.items,
    variants: Array.from(allVariants.values()),
  })

  return { items }
}

const formatInventoryInput = ({
  product_variant_inventory_items,
  location_ids,
  items,
  stockAvailability,
  variants,
}: ConfirmInventoryPreparationInput) => {
  if (!product_variant_inventory_items.length) {
    return []
  }

  const variantsMap = new Map<
    string,
    ConfirmInventoryPreparationInput["variants"][0]
  >(variants.map((v) => [v.id, v]))

  const itemsToConfirm: ConfirmInventoryItem[] = []

  items.forEach((item) => {
    const variant = variantsMap.get(item.variant_id!)

    if (!variant?.manage_inventory) {
      return
    }

    const variantInventoryItems = product_variant_inventory_items.filter(
      (i) => i.variant_id === item.variant_id
    )

    if (!variantInventoryItems.length) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        `Variant ${item.variant_id} does not have any inventory items associated with it.`
      )
    }

    variantInventoryItems.forEach((variantInventoryItem) => {
      const locationsWithAvailability = location_ids.filter((locId) =>
        MathBN.gte(
          stockAvailability
            .get(locId)
            ?.get(variantInventoryItem.inventory_item_id) ?? 0,
          MathBN.mult(variantInventoryItem.required_quantity, item.quantity)
        )
      )

      const locationsWithLevel = location_ids.filter((locId) =>
        stockAvailability
          .get(locId)
          ?.has(variantInventoryItem.inventory_item_id)
      )

      itemsToConfirm.push({
        id: item.id,
        inventory_item_id: variantInventoryItem.inventory_item_id,
        required_quantity: variantInventoryItem.required_quantity,
        allow_backorder: !!variant.allow_backorder,
        quantity: item.quantity,
        location_ids: locationsWithAvailability.length
          ? locationsWithAvailability
          : locationsWithLevel.length
          ? locationsWithLevel
          : location_ids,
      })
    })
  })

  return itemsToConfirm
}

        quantity: MathBN.mult(item.required_quantity, item.quantity),
        allow_backorder: item.allow_backorder,
        location_id: item.location_ids[0],
      }
    })

    const lockingKeys = Array.from(new Set(inventoryItemIds))

    const reservations = await locking.execute(lockingKeys, async () => {
      return await inventoryService.createReservationItems(items)
    })

    return new StepResponse(reservations, {
      reservations: reservations.map((r) => r.id),
      inventoryItemIds,
    })

    if (!data?.reservations?.length) {
      return

    const locking = container.resolve(Modules.LOCKING)

    const inventoryItemIds = data.inventoryItemIds
    const lockingKeys = Array.from(new Set(inventoryItemIds))

    await locking.execute(lockingKeys, async () => {
      await inventoryService.deleteReservationItems(data.reservations)
    })

    return new StepResponse()
  }

type TotalVariantAvailabilityData = {
  variant_ids: string[]
}

/**
 * Computes the total availability for a list of variants across all stock locations
 *
 * @param query - The Query function
 * @param data - An object containing the variant ids to compute the availability for
 * @returns the total availability for the given variants
 */
export async function getTotalVariantAvailability(
  query: Omit<RemoteQueryFunction, symbol>,
  data: TotalVariantAvailabilityData
): Promise<{
  [variant_id: string]: {
    availability: number | null
  }
}> {
  const { variantInventoriesMap, locationIds } = await getDataForComputation(
    query,
    data
  )

  return data.variant_ids.reduce((acc, variantId) => {
    const variantInventoryItems = variantInventoriesMap.get(variantId) || []
    acc[variantId] = {
      availability: computeVariantAvailability(
        variantInventoryItems,
        locationIds,
        { requireChannelCheck: false }
      ),
    }
    return acc
  }, {})
}

interface VariantItems {
  variant_id: string
  required_quantity: number
  variant: {
    manage_inventory: boolean
    allow_backorder: boolean
  }
  inventory: {
    location_levels: {
      location_id: string
      available_quantity: number
    }[]
  }
}

const computeVariantAvailability = (
  variantInventoryItems: VariantItems[],
  channelLocationsSet: Set<string>,
  { requireChannelCheck } = { requireChannelCheck: true }
): number | null => {
  const inventoryQuantities: number[] = []

  for (const link of variantInventoryItems) {
    const requiredQuantity = link.required_quantity
    const availableQuantity = (link.inventory?.location_levels || []).reduce(
      (sum, level) => {
        if (
          requireChannelCheck &&
          !channelLocationsSet.has(level.location_id)
        ) {
          return sum
        }

        return sum + (level?.available_quantity || 0)
      },
      0
    )

    // This will give us the maximum deliverable quantities for each inventory item
    const maxInventoryQuantity = Math.floor(
      availableQuantity / requiredQuantity
    )

    inventoryQuantities.push(maxInventoryQuantity)
  }

  return inventoryQuantities.length ? Math.min(...inventoryQuantities) : null
}

type VariantAvailabilityData = {
  variant_ids: string[]
  sales_channel_id: string
}

const getDataForComputation = async (
  query: Omit<RemoteQueryFunction, symbol>,
  data: { variant_ids: string[]; sales_channel_id?: string }
) => {
  const { data: variantInventoryItems } = await query.graph(
    {
      entity: "product_variant_inventory_items",

        "variant_id",

      ],
      filters: { variant_id: data.variant_ids },

    {

        enable: true,
      },
    }
  )

  const variantInventoriesMap = new Map()
  variantInventoryItems.forEach((link) => {
    const array = variantInventoriesMap.get(link.variant_id) || []
    array.push(link)
    variantInventoriesMap.set(link.variant_id, array)
  })

  const locationIds = new Set<string>()
  if (data.sales_channel_id) {

    req.queryConfig.fields = req.queryConfig.fields.filter(

    )

    filters["sales_channels"]["id"] = salesChannelIds

    delete filters.sales_channel_id

    filters["variants"] ??= {}
  }

    {
      entity: "product",
      fields: req.queryConfig.fields,
      filters,
      pagination: req.queryConfig.pagination,
      context,
    },

  - Link the key with `POST /admin/api-keys/:id/sales-channels { add: [...] }`.
  - Create a stock location, then link it with `POST /admin/stock-locations/:id/sales-channels`.

import { ModuleJoinerConfig } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { LINKS, Modules } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"

export const ProductVariantInventoryItem: ModuleJoinerConfig = {
  serviceName: LINKS.ProductVariantInventoryItem,
  isLink: true,
  databaseConfig: {
    tableName: "product_variant_inventory_item",
    idPrefix: "pvitem",
    extraFields: {
      required_quantity: {
        type: "integer",

All paths below are under `/Users/loganfecko/Desktop/CSCI_435/medusa/packages`. Line numbers come from direct reads or greps, except a few marked "approx". I only read files and wrote nothing.

## 1. How inventory kits work today

**The link.**
- The definition is `modules/link-modules/src/definitions/product-variant-inventory-item.ts`.
- The table is `product_variant_inventory_item`, id prefix `pvitem`, and the primary keys are `id, variant_id, inventory_item_id`.
- It has an extra column `required_quantity` (integer, default "1").
- You can query it as `product_variant_inventory_items`. Fields are `variant_id`, `inventory_item_id`, `required_quantity` and the `variant.*` and `inventory.*` relations.
- A variant therefore links to many inventory items. One inventory item can also link to many variants.

**`createProductsWorkflow`.**
- The file is `core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/create-products.ts`.
- `validateProductInputStep` (about line 73) only requires that each product has options.
- Variants are stripped from the product input at lines 170-177.
- `createProductVariantsWorkflow.runAsStep(variantsInput)` is called at about lines 223-247.
- The `productsCreated` hook is at about line 281, and it receives `{products, additional_data}`.

**`createProductVariantsWorkflow`.**
- The file is `core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/create-product-variants.ts`.
- The input type has `inventory_items?: {inventory_item_id, required_quantity?}[]` (lines 48-60).
- `validateInventoryItems` (from `inventory/steps/validate-inventory-items.ts`) checks that the item ids exist. It is called at about line 271.
- `buildVariantItemCreateMap` (line 164) auto-creates a default inventory item only when the variant has `manage_inventory` and no `inventory_items` were passed.
- `buildLinksToCreate` (line 112) calls `buildLink` (line 64). `required_quantity` defaults to 1 (line 155).
- `createInventoryItemsWorkflow.runAsStep` is at about line 278, and `createLinksWorkflow.runAsStep` is at about line 304.
- The `productVariantsCreated` hook is at about line 364.

**Admin routes.**
- Create link: `medusa/src/api/admin/products/[id]/variants/[variant_id]/inventory-items/route.ts`.
  - POST calls `createLinksWorkflow` with `{[Modules.PRODUCT]:{variant_id}, [Modules.INVENTORY]:{inventory_item_id}, data:{required_quantity}}`.
- Update and delete link: `.../inventory-items/[inventory_item_id]/route.ts`.
  - POST uses `updateLinksWorkflow`.
  - DELETE uses `dismissLinksWorkflow` and returns `{id, object:"variant-inventory-item-link", deleted, parent}`.
- Batch: `medusa/src/api/admin/products/[id]/variants/inventory-items/batch/route.ts`.
  - It calls `batchLinksWorkflow` (`core/core-flows/src/common/workflows/batch-links.ts`).
  - The input is built by `buildBatchVariantInventoryData` in `medusa/src/api/admin/products/helpers.ts:215-238`.
- Generic link workflows live in `core/core-flows/src/common/workflows/{create,update,dismiss,batch}-links.ts`.
- Inventory item workflows are in `core/core-flows/src/inventory/workflows/` (`create-inventory-items.ts`, `delete-inventory-items.ts`, and others).
- `dismissProductVariantsInventoryStep` is in `core/core-flows/src/product/steps/`. `updateProductsWorkflow` uses it when `manage_inventory` is set to false.

**Validators and types.**
- Zod schemas are in `medusa/src/api/admin/products/validators.ts`.
  - `CreateProductVariant.inventory_items` is at lines 181-187. `required_quantity` is `z.number()`, so it is not validated as positive or an integer.
  - Link schemas are at lines 343-393.
- HttpTypes are in `core/types/src/http/product/admin/payloads.ts`.
  - `AdminCreateProductVariantInventoryKit` is at line 99, with the `inventory_items` field at line 182.
  - The link payload types are at lines 668-706 and 822-843.
- `AdminProductVariantInventoryItemLink` (`required_quantity`, `inventory`) is in `core/types/src/http/product/admin/entitites.ts:19-66`.

**Duplicate product.** `core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/duplicate-product.ts` (comment at about lines 240-262) creates fresh inventory items with no stock. A bundle copy would not keep its component links unless that workflow is changed.

## 2. Reservation at order placement (verified)

`required_quantity * line quantity` is applied in all three places:
- `core/core-flows/src/cart/utils/prepare-confirm-inventory-input.ts`
  - It pulls the required fields from the variant's `inventory_items` (lines 12-48).
  - `formatInventoryInput` creates one `itemsToConfirm` entry per variant inventory item (about lines 215-280).
  - Location selection at line 258 uses `MathBN.gte(available, MathBN.mult(required_quantity, item.quantity))`.
  - It throws an error if the variant has no inventory items.
  - It skips variants where `manage_inventory` is false.
- `core/core-flows/src/cart/steps/confirm-inventory.ts:80` is `MathBN.mult(item.quantity, item.required_quantity)`, passed to `inventoryService.confirmInventory`. Backorder is skipped.
- `core/core-flows/src/cart/steps/reserve-inventory.ts:82` is `quantity: MathBN.mult(item.required_quantity, item.quantity)`.
  - It creates reservation items under the `locking` module, using the inventory item ids as keys. The compensation deletes the reservations.
- `core/core-flows/src/cart/workflows/complete-cart.ts`
  - `prepareConfirmInventoryInput` is at line 554.
  - `reserveInventoryStep(formatedInventoryItems)` is at line 639, inside `parallelize`.
- Reservations are per inventory item, each tied to `line_item_id`.
- `core/core-flows/src/cart/workflows/confirm-variant-inventory.ts:147` also uses `confirmInventoryStep`.
- The order fulfillment, return and claim workflows also read `required_quantity` (`order/utils/fields.ts` and others).

## 3. Availability

- `core/utils/src/product/get-variant-availability.ts`
  - `computeVariantAvailability` (about lines 114-147) sums `location_levels.available_quantity` for each link.
  - Locations are restricted to the sales channel's stock locations, unless `requireChannelCheck` is false.
  - Each link gives `Math.floor(available / required_quantity)` (line 139).
  - The result is `Math.min(...)` over the links, or `null` if there are none (line 146).
  - `getVariantAvailability` takes a sales channel. `getTotalVariantAvailability` (about line 68) covers all locations.
  - Both read `product_variant_inventory_items` with `cache: {enable: true}` (about line 150). Staleness is a consideration for bundles.
- `medusa/src/api/utils/middlewares/products/variant-inventory-quantity.ts`
  - `wrapVariantsWithInventoryQuantityForSalesChannel` (line 28) needs exactly one sales channel, from the publishable key or the request.
  - `wrapVariantsWithTotalInventoryQuantity` is at line 10.
  - `wrapVariants` (line 76) skips variants where `manage_inventory` is false.
- `medusa/src/api/store/products/route.ts` removes `variants.inventory_quantity` from the query fields and then calls the wrapper (lines 40-47, 90 and 114-147). `store/products/[id]/route.ts` and `store/product-variants/*` do the same.
- The admin product list does not use this path.

## 4. Create, update and delete workflows and hooks

# Plan: #112 Add API to create and manage product bundles (part 1 of #101)

## Context
#101 (product bundles with their own price) was split into sub-issues. #112 is the backend foundation:
admin create/update API, store API exposure, stock behaviour, and delete guards. Later sub-issues
(checkout errors, refund shares/returns, admin UI) depend on it. #112 states: no new data model, no migration,
built on existing inventory-kit links (`product_variant_inventory_item` with `required_quantity`).

Customer decisions already on #101: returns refund proportional to component normal price (later issue);
deleting a component is BLOCKED and names the bundles; a bundle is a normal product in the store API
(own title/images/price/categories); bundle pages/upsells out of scope.

## What already works (no change needed)
- Reservation at cart completion multiplies `required_quantity * line qty` per inventory item
  (`core-flows/src/cart/utils/prepare-confirm-inventory-input.ts`, `steps/reserve-inventory.ts`). AC5 comes for free
  if the bundle variant is linked to the component inventory items.
- Store availability = min over links of floor(available / required_quantity)
  (`packages/core/utils/src/product/get-variant-availability.ts`). AC6 comes for free. Note: link read is cached.
- Prices per currency on a variant (AC1/AC10): a bundle variant has its own prices, independent of components.

## Design
**Model (no migration):** a bundle = one product, one variant (`manage_inventory: true`, own prices).
- Variant is linked to the component inventory items. For each component (variant_id, quantity), resolve the
  component variant's inventory items and link with `required_quantity = quantity * component link required_quantity`;
  merge by `inventory_item_id` (sum) if components share an item.
- Component list is stored in `product.metadata.bundle = { components: [{ variant_id, quantity }] }`.
  Needed because merged inventory links cannot be turned back into variant+quantity. `metadata` is already a json column.
- Reserved key: reject plain product create/update that sets `metadata.bundle`, so only the bundle API writes it.

**Routes** (new group, `packages/medusa/src/api/admin/bundles/`): `POST /admin/bundles` (create),
`POST /admin/bundles/:id` (update). Same auth/policy middleware pattern as
`packages/medusa/src/api/admin/products/middlewares.ts`; registered in `packages/medusa/src/api/middlewares.ts`.
Zod validators: title etc. reuse product schemas; `components` min 2, `quantity` int >= 1, `prices` non-empty, amount >= 0.

**Workflows** (`packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/`):
- `create-bundle.ts`: `validateBundleComponentsStep` -> build product input -> `createProductsWorkflow.runAsStep`
  (inventory links through the variant `inventory_items` input). Nested workflow compensation gives AC8.
  Expose a `bundleCreated` hook.
- `update-bundle.ts`: validate -> `updateProductsWorkflow` (fields, prices, metadata) -> diff and rewrite
  links (`batchLinksWorkflow`). Hook `bundleUpdated`.
- Pure helpers (unit-testable) in `product/utils/`: `validateBundleComponents`, `buildBundleInventoryLinks`.
  Validation: >= 2 components, no duplicate variant, quantity > 0, variants exist, `manage_inventory` true and has
  inventory items, component product is not itself a bundle. Errors via `MedusaError(INVALID_DATA | NOT_FOUND)`.

**Delete guard (AC11):** new `validateNoBundleUsageStep` inserted right after the initial query in
`delete-products.ts` and `delete-product-variants.ts` (both run the admin DELETE routes and the batch routes).
It loads bundle products, finds those whose `metadata.bundle.components` reference any variant being deleted
(excluding bundles being deleted in the same call), and throws `NOT_ALLOWED` naming every bundle (title + id).
Deleting the bundle itself is allowed (proposed answer to the open question: orders keep line-item copies).

**Store (AC3/AC4):** bundles are ordinary products so listing and detail already work. Add a `bundle` field
(`{ components: [{ variant_id, quantity }] }`) to store product responses, present only for bundle products,
derived from metadata in the store product routes (`store/products/route.ts`, `[id]/route.ts`). Default store
fields otherwise unchanged so non-bundle responses are identical (AC13).

**Types / SDK:** `AdminCreateBundle`, `AdminUpdateBundle`, response types in `packages/core/types/src/http/product/admin/`;
`StoreProduct.bundle` in the store types. Add a changeset.

## Test plan: every acceptance criterion has an explicit test
Unit (Jest, `packages/core/core-flows/src/product/utils/__tests__/bundle.spec.ts`, modelled on
`prepare-confirm-inventory-input.spec.ts` using `expect(...).toThrow(MedusaError)`):
| AC | Test |
|----|------|
| 7 | one `it` per rejection: <2 components, missing variant, no inventory tracking, component is a bundle, duplicate, qty 0 / negative |
| 1,5 | `buildBundleInventoryLinks`: required_quantity = qty * component required_quantity; shared items summed |

HTTP integration (`integration-tests/http/__tests__/product/admin/bundle.spec.ts`; seeding as in
`product/admin/variant.spec.ts` and `product/store/product.spec.ts`; run `yarn test:integration:http`):
| AC | Test |
|----|------|
| 1 | create "Camera kit" with title/images/category, 3 components, USD 899 + EUR 849; 200, product, prices and links present |
| 2 | update title, swap a component, change quantity and price; links and metadata reflect it |
| 3 | store GET product by id and by category list returns the kit with title, images, price, categories |
| 4 | store product has `bundle.components`; a normal product has no `bundle` |
| 5 | add to cart, complete; GET `/admin/reservations` shows each component reserved at qty * bundles ordered (2 bundles -> 2x) |
| 6 | component stock 0 -> store inventory_quantity 0; stocks 10/7/3 with qty 1/2/1 -> 3 (floor min) |
| 7 | each rejection returns 400/404 with a clear message (same cases, via API) |
| 8 | failing `bundleCreated` hook handler: afterwards no product, variant, link or metadata left over |
| 9 | no auth header -> 401 on create and update |
| 10 | change a component variant price; bundle price unchanged |
| 11 | delete component product -> error naming bundle(s); same for variant; two bundles -> both named; after removing from bundles, delete succeeds |
| 12 | order a bundle, then edit and delete the bundle; order still retrieves, fulfils and can be returned |
| 13 | existing product/variant/inventory/cart suites pass unchanged; no migration file added (check `git diff --stat`) |

## Risks / items to verify while implementing
1. AC12: deleting a bundle variant dismisses its inventory links; fulfilment/returns read `required_quantity` from
   those links (`order/utils/fields.ts`). Order fulfilment after bundle delete may break. Needs an early spike;
   if so, the fix (snapshot at order time, or soft-delete handling) may expand scope. Raise on the issue if needed.
2. Delete guard looks up bundles via JSON metadata. Confirm query-graph can filter on `metadata`; otherwise load
   products with metadata and filter in memory (fine at current scale, note it).
3. A component's inventory kit changing later does not update bundle links (not covered by spec; flag in issue).
4. `duplicate-product.ts` drops links, so duplicating a bundle yields a broken bundle. Block duplication of bundles.
5. Dismissing a link or deleting an inventory item directly is unguarded; out of #112 scope, note it.
6. `required_quantity` on the existing link route is only `z.number()`; our new routes validate integer >= 1 themselves.
7. Open questions to answer on #112: max components (propose cap, e.g. 20, or none); deleting a bundle with unfulfilled
   orders (propose allowed).

## Housekeeping
Working tree on `chore/lefecko-sprint3-checkin` holds unrelated uncommitted product-activity work and macOS "file 2/3"
duplicates. Implement in a new worktree/branch off `develop` and do not stage those files.

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: #112 Add API to create and manage product bundles (part 1 of #101)

## Context
#101 (product bundles with their own price) was split into sub-issues. #112 is the backend foundation:
admin create/update API, store API exposure, stock behaviour, and delete guards. Later sub-issues
(checkout errors, refund shares/returns, admin UI) depend on it. #112 states: no new data model, no migration,
built on existing inventory-kit links (`product_variant_inventory_item` with `required_quantity`).

Customer decisions already on #101: returns refund proportional to component normal price (later issue);
deleting a component is BLOCKED and names the bundles; a bundle is a normal product in the store API
(own title/images/price/categories); bundle pages/upsells out of scope.

## What already works (no change needed)
- Reservation at cart completion multiplies `required_quantity * line qty` per inventory item
  (`core-flows/src/cart/utils/prepare-confirm-inventory-input.ts`, `steps/reserve-inventory.ts`). AC5 comes for free
  if the bundle variant is linked to the component inventory items.
- Store availability = min over links of floor(available / required_quantity)
  (`packages/core/utils/src/product/get-variant-availability.ts`). AC6 comes for free. Note: link read is cached.
- Prices per currency on a variant (AC1/AC10): a bundle variant has its own prices, independent of components.

## Design
**Model (no migration):** a bundle = one product, one variant (`manage_inventory: true`, own prices).
- Variant is linked to the component inventory items. For each component (variant_id, quantity), resolve the
  component variant's inventory items and link with `required_quantity = quantity * component link required_quantity`;
  merge by `inventory_item_id` (sum) if components share an item.
- Component list is stored in `product.metadata.bundle = { components: [{ variant_id, quantity }] }`.
  Needed because merged inventory links cannot be turned back into variant+quantity. `metadata` is already a json column.
- Reserved key: reject plain product create/update that sets `metadata.bundle`, so only the bundle API writes it.

**Routes** (new group, `packages/medusa/src/api/admin/bundles/`): `POST /admin/bundles` (create),
`POST /admin/bundles/:id` (update). Same auth/policy middleware pattern as
`packages/medusa/src/api/admin/products/middlewares.ts`; registered in `packages/medusa/src/api/middlewares.ts`.
Zod validators: title etc. reuse product schemas; `components` min 2, `quantity` int >= 1, `prices` non-empty, amount >= 0.

**Workflows** (`packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/`):
- `create-bundle.ts`: `validateBundleComponentsStep` -> build product input -> `createProductsWorkflow.runAsStep`
  (inventory links through the variant `inventory_items` input). Nested workflow compensation gives AC8.
  Expose a `bundleCreated` hook.
- `update-bundle.ts`: validate -> `updateProductsWorkflow` (fields, prices, metadata) -> diff and rewrite
  links (`batchLinksWorkflow`). Hook `bundleUpdated`.
- Pure helpers (unit-testable) in `product/utils/`: `validateBundleComponents`, `buildBundleInventoryLinks`.
  Validation: >= 2 components, no duplicate variant, quantity > 0, variants exist, `manage_inventory` true and has
  inventory items, component product is not itself a bundle. Errors via `MedusaError(INVALID_DATA | NOT_FOUND)`.

**Delete guard (AC11):** new `validateNoBundleUsageStep` inserted right after the initial query in
`delete-products.ts` and `delete-product-variants.ts` (both run the admin DELETE routes and the batch routes).
It loads bundle products, finds those whose `metadata.bundle.components` reference any variant being deleted
(excluding bundles being deleted in the same call), and throws `NOT_ALLOWED` naming every bundle (title + id).
Deleting the bundle itself is allowed (proposed answer to the open question: orders keep line-item copies).

**Store (AC3/AC4):** bundles are ordinary products so listing and detail already work. Add a `bundle` field
(`{ components: [{ variant_id, quantity }] }`) to store product responses, present only for bundle products,
derived from metadata in the store product routes (`store/products/route.ts`, `[id]/route.ts`). Default store
fields otherwise unchanged so non-bundle responses are identical (AC13).

**Types / SDK:** `AdminCreateBundle`, `AdminUpdateBundle`, response types in `packages/core/types/src/http/product/admin/`;
`StoreProduct.bundle` in the store types. Add a changeset.

## Test plan: every acceptance criterion has an explicit test
Unit (Jest, `packages/core/core-flows/src/product/utils/__tests__/bundle.spec.ts`, modelled on
`prepare-confirm-inventory-input.spec.ts` using `expect(...).toThrow(MedusaError)`):
| AC | Test |
|----|------|
| 7 | one `it` per rejection: <2 components, missing variant, no inventory tracking, component is a bundle, duplicate, qty 0 / negative |
| 1,5 | `buildBundleInventoryLinks`: required_quantity = qty * component required_quantity; shared items summed |

HTTP integration (`integration-tests/http/__tests__/product/admin/bundle.spec.ts`; seeding as in
`product/admin/variant.spec.ts` and `product/store/product.spec.ts`; run `yarn test:integration:http`):
| AC | Test |
|----|------|
| 1 | create "Camera kit" with title/images/category, 3 components, USD 899 + EUR 849; 200, product, prices and links present |
| 2 | update title, swap a component, change quantity and price; links and metadata reflect it |
| 3 | store GET product by id and by category list returns the kit with title, images, price, categories |
| 4 | store product has `bundle.components`; a normal product has no `bundle` |
| 5 | add to cart, complete; GET `/admin/reservations` shows each component reserved at qty * bundles ordered (2 bundles -> 2x) |
| 6 | component stock 0 -> store inventory_quantity 0; stocks 10/7/3 with qty 1/2/1 -> 3 (floor min) |
| 7 | each rejection returns 400/404 with a clear message (same cases, via API) |
| 8 | failing `bundleCreated` hook handler: afterwards no product, variant, link or metadata left over |
| 9 | no auth header -> 401 on create and update |
| 10 | change a component variant price; bundle price unchanged |
| 11 | delete component product -> error naming bundle(s); same for variant; two bundles -> both named; after removing from bundles, delete succeeds |
| 12 | order a bundle, then edit and delete the bundle; order still retrieves, fulfils and can be returned |
| 13 | existing product/variant/inventory/cart suites pass unchanged; no migration file added (check `git diff --stat`) |

## Risks / items to verify while implementing
1. AC12: deleting a bundle variant dismisses its inventory links; fulfilment/returns read `required_quantity` from
   those links (`order/utils/fields.ts`). Order fulfilment after bundle delete may break. Needs an early spike;
   if so, the fix (snapshot at order time, or soft-delete handling) may expand scope. Raise on the issue if needed.
2. Delete guard looks up bundles via JSON metadata. Confirm query-graph can filter on `metadata`; otherwise load
   products with metadata and filter in memory (fine at current scale, note it).
3. A component's inventory kit changing later does not update bundle links (not covered by spec; flag in issue).
4. `duplicate-product.ts` drops links, so duplicating a bundle yields a broken bundle. Block duplication of bundles.
5. Dismissing a link or deleting an inventory item directly is unguarded; out of #112 scope, note it.
6. `required_quantity` on the existing link route is only `z.number()`; our new routes validate integer >= 1 themselves.
7. Open questions to answer on #112: max components (propose cap, e.g. 20, or none); deleting a bundle with unfulfilled
   orders (propose allowed).
